name: Trihexyphenidyl
mechanism: Antimuscarinic that reduces cholinergic activity in the CNS
dosing: Start 1 mg two or three times daily, titrate cautiously; doses vary (specialist guidance recommended)
contraindications: Narrow-angle glaucoma, urinary retention, severe prostatic hypertrophy, severe dementia
interactions: Other anticholinergics (additive effects), may antagonise acetylcholinesterase inhibitors
monitoring: Cognitive status, urinary retention, bowel function, temperature in hot weather
sideEffects: Confusion, dry mouth, blurred vision, urinary retention, constipation, tachycardia, hallucinations
clinicalPearls: Sometimes helpful for tremor in younger patients but generally poorly tolerated in older adults; use with caution in the elderly due to cognitive adverse effects.
indication: Symptomatic management of tremor in Parkinson's disease (selected patients)
